Releases

0.2.1 #

Released 2026-11-05. The GitHub release

Added #

  • tests/run.sh --changed-from REF (or --changed-files FILE, one path per line) adds to the fast tier the steps whose covers globs match a file changed since REF (git diff REF...HEAD) and those whose command names a changed file; a step with no covers is not added by its globs. --plan prints the selection and the shard plan and runs nothing, and a sharded run ends with a shard i/K: planned Ns, the steps took Ns together line.
  • tests/durations.txt holds the recorded duration of every step, from a whole run, for --shard i/K --durations tests/durations.txt: the four parts of the suite plan within 1.3 times of each other (CONTRIBUTING, Tests, says how to regenerate it). tests/test_ci.py checks the CI workflow and the shard balance.
  • The methodology parameter ci_timeout_minutes (default 30; a positive whole number, a parameter may carry a pattern) sets the timeout-minutes of the CI job the gitflow scaffold writes, so a project sets it from its own suite budgets.
  • qargi release status shows, in the suite record's verdict, how long the run took and the mode its command names (-j N, shard I/K): pass at this head (command: C; ran AT; took 412s; -j 8). release verify and feature verify record both; a record made before shows the command and the time only.
  • Catalog entries for common development tooling, found with qargi discover search and installed as role packages: pkg-golangci-lint, pkg-bats, pkg-podman, pkg-mandoc, pkg-golang (the Go toolchain and a C compiler, so go test -race runs) and pkg-gh (the GitHub command line, for its release commands). A test checks every entry of the shipped catalog against the schema of its kind.
  • qargi project profile check [NAME] [--profile FILE] (read only, so a member may run it) reads a repository's profile (~/.qargi/config/profiles/<repository>.md, the repository being the project's directory name, or FILE). It exits 1 while the profile still carries the shipped example's title or "Copy to" line, and warns (exit 0) of each backticked command in the profile's Gates section that is in none of the repository's CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and Makefile targets. No profile is fine. project validate prints the header finding as a WARN: line.
  • roles.ROLE.tools: the tools a role needs beyond its apt packages, declared once in the project's answers as a list of {kind, name, ...} entries. go (a package path and a tagged version: go install NAME@VERSION), binary (a file name, version, the URL of the file and its sha256: downloaded to ~/.local/bin and kept only when the hash matches) and submodule (a name and the path of a submodule of the repository). project validate checks each kind's keys and that two roles do not pin one tool differently. qargi env plan lists every tool with its state here (ok, missing, wrong, path) and the token covers the list; qargi env apply installs the go tools (go must be in --approve-exec) and binaries that are missing or wrong, after the bootstrap, and records them; qargi env check reports a tool that is not installed, is another version (go version -m) or another file (sha256), sits in a directory PATH lacks, or a declared submodule that is not initialised or at another commit. qargi local prepare checks the role's declared submodules out in the member's clone from the lead's copy of their objects, offline (a mirror with no remote under RUN/sub, push URL disabled) and prints SUBMODULES=path,...; a commit the lead's copy lacks, a submodule not initialised there, or a run made with --repo-url, is a note and nothing is fetched (lib/tools.py).
  • Providers as data, one runtime per surface. Claude ships as two runtimes of one family, claude-code (local) and claude-platform (cloud), with a shared model catalog. The family name claude resolves per surface (a notice says so) in a project's models.provider and in provider of; every provider verb that takes a NAME takes a runtime name (there is no runtime named claude). Definitions follow schema-2.json: tiers with the date and source each model was verified, effort levels, a capability matrix, a layout (skills, agents, settings, memory, transcripts, render target, launch line; a verb that needs a facility the runtime lacks says provider NAME has no FACILITY, exit 3), a renderer for the member file, a dispatch (in-session or a command), a barrier and notes.
  • models.provider per surface: qargi project set P models.provider.local|cloud NAME (a runtime that does not serve that surface is refused, exit 2), and project new|attach take --provider NAME or --provider-local and --provider-cloud; nothing is guessed. project validate, init, attach and new print finding: models.provider is not set (exit status unchanged); a verb that needs a surface the answers leave out exits 2 and says which.
  • Provider notes: a definition's notes (up to 16 topics, one line each, plain text) say what the skills would otherwise have to say about the runtime. qargi provider notes [TOPIC] [--project P] [--surface cloud] prints one of the project's runtime (exit 1 for a topic it lacks, exit 2 for a project with no runtime or one that cannot be used as it stands). provider check fails a bad note and warns when an in-session local runtime has no spawn note; an extension cannot add notes. claude-code ships spawn, session-model, exploration, skills-dir, identity and commands; claude-platform ships output-dir and clone-dir.
  • Contract addenda: a definition lists resources.contract_addenda, text files of its own directory (16 KB each, no control or format characters) that are added to a member's contract, so the neutral contract never names a surface. claude-platform carries cloud-run.md (the detached-gate recipe, the no-wrapper git case, /workspace/<repo>, /mnt/session/outputs); claude-code carries local-run.md (background commands, Monitor, no foreground sleep). qargi provider addenda NAME SURFACE prints them. A cloud agent's prompt is the contract, the output format and the addenda of the project's cloud runtime (the prompt hash covers them); local prepare copies the local runtime's into the run's CONTRACT directory as runtime-addenda.md. instances refresh-prompt stops with could not render the system prompt when an addendum cannot be read.
  • Provider packs in the library: qargi provider new|import|seal|remove|enable|disable|attest for provider, catalog and extension packs, each a plan, a token and your approval, with --approve-exec naming every executable. A pack holds text only (binaries, archives, links and secrets are refused). A pack counts only while it is what you sealed, and a capability counts only with a verified.json record bound to the definition's hash, written by provider check (hermetic cases) or provider attest (asked each time; it never runs or spends anything). A name defined both shipped and in the library is refused. The conformance harness is lib/conformance/ (tests/conformance.sh still runs it).
  • Extensions: a project's models.extensions compose onto its runtime; two that provide the same thing, or one that collides with the runtime, are refused, and an extension's capability counts only after provider check or attest of it passes. provider show|check|layout|require-skills|launch --project P and provider effective ... --project P show the composed view, and agent for, provider accept, session and provision read it. A member whose text depends on an extension shows STALE until qargi agent refresh.
  • qargi provider adapter-run NAME SURFACE VERB [--check] runs a verb of a runtime's adapter (a library adapter only as a sealed private copy; a verb the definition does not list exits 3), and qargi provider model NAME SURFACE TIER prints a tier's model.
  • qargi local run RUN [--dry-run] runs a task through a runtime whose dispatch is a command (a vendor CLI): the argv comes from the definition, with no shell and a scrubbed environment (only the names in dispatch.env_pass, shown in the review), and the output goes to OUT/transcript. It builds from the project's composed definition; a read-only run is refused when the barrier comes from an extension, or the runtime's own barrier is a hook or adapter, unless the project recorded provider accept. A runtime that works inside the session is refused.
  • qargi project link|unlink PROJECT [--resource skills,agents,memory]: one plan and token links the project's skills, agents and memory into the work tree, each as the runtime's definition says (a directory link, one link per entry, or a copy; the memory directory becomes a link into ~/.qargi/memory/projects/PROJECT). A real directory in the way moves to NAME.qargi-backup.
  • qargi packs link|unlink PROJECT: the project's skills directory in the repository becomes a link to the render of packs apply --target, so a session in the checkout loads the packs without --add-dir. The plan lists what a real directory there holds (same as the library, differs, or new); apply moves it to skills.qargi-backup, unlink moves it back (also when the link is already gone); nothing is deleted. A foreign link, a symlinked parent, files tracked by git and a missing render are refused.
  • qargi packs check --target ends with the skills a session would load, each qargi, accepted, drifted, excluded or unmanaged (only drifted changes the exit status), says when the checkout is not linked, and reads the exclusion from the runtime's settings in every form. qargi skill accept|unaccept PROJECT NAME [--user] records a skill qargi does not manage, by name and content hash. project attach hints when the repository has its own skills.
  • Members are rendered from one neutral definition (agents/member.json, member.body.md) through the runtime's renderer. agent list and agent models show STALE (definition, catalog, renderer or an enabled extension changed) and DRIFT (file edited by hand).
  • The render of a member is kept in the configuration directory, ~/.qargi/config/agents/PROJECT/NAME.EXT (beside agents.json, outside every repository), and the runtime's file is written from it: agent add, rename and refresh write both, remove deletes both. A checkout that is cleaned or cloned afresh gets its members back with qargi agent refresh NAME --project P, which also hides the file from git again. agent list and agent models show MISSING (the runtime's file is gone), STALE (the copy in config is gone or changed, or the inputs of the render did) or DRIFT (the file was edited by hand), each with that command. env check reads the new form.
  • Every skill and tool pack declares compatible_providers (runtime names, family names or any) as part of its content hash: skill|tool new|import --compatible LIST and seal --compatible. A project's runtime skips a pack it is not on, with a note in effective, check, packs apply|check|link and discover install [--compatible].
  • The member guard takes its hook protocol and protected directories from the provider definitions (qargi __guard --provider NAME).
  • qargi help guard says in one place what a local member's guard refuses and what it allows, and qargi help approvals says that a token covers the plan seen, that --approved is recorded and not verified, that gated verbs are never allow-listed and that a member never applies. The manual page has a GUARD section.
  • qargi project validate prints a WARN: line for each pack linked to a role of the project that is not in the pack library. packs check --target and skill|tool check PROJECT ROLE print no pack is linked to any role of PROJECT when none is.
  • qargi marshal handoff [NAME] [--write FILE] [--json]: a read-only note for a fresh session, built from stored facts only (repository, HEAD, base, host, features, the marshal record, the packs check and launch line, the last env check and env apply), with the lead-only qargi-session skill.
  • qargi marshal claim NAME --as-successor-of ID: a lead session that was restarted continues as the lead, without the owner's takeover, when the record's lead is ID, its lease is stale and the host, OS user and work tree are the same. Anything else stays the owner's takeover. feature start continues the same way, and marshal status, marshal check and marshal handoff name the command.
  • qargi lead usage [--project P] [--session ID | --transcript FILE] [--json] says how much of the lead session's context is in use. qargi lead compact-check [--advise] [--json] says whether a /compact is safe now (exit 0) or not (exit 1) with every reason (an open local run, a merge waiting in the conflicts directory, a whole-suite run in progress, a handoff note older than the last merge, an open release or hotfix branch) and prints what to re-read after it. The window is the project answer lead.context_window (default: the runtime's resources.transcripts, which claude-code ships). qargi cannot run /compact.
  • feature finish, the feature merge that closes a feature's last open run, release finish and marshal handoff end with lead: N% context; compact is safe now: run /compact (or why not) at or above the answer lead.compact_advice_pct (default 40; 0 turns it off). They never fail or wait for it.
  • qargi env show [--project P] [--repo DIR] [--json] prints what a repository declares about its development environment, read as text from files it already has: the AGENTS.md or README.md section headed Development environment, Environment or Setup; version pins (go.mod, .tool-versions, mise.toml, .python-version, .nvmrc, package.json engines); .gitmodules; the bootstrap and doctor targets of a Makefile, justfile, Taskfile or mise tasks; a devcontainer. It derives the doctor, bootstrap and dry-run commands. The project answers env.doctor_command, env.bootstrap_command, env.dry_run_command and env.known_failures override them. A member may run it. See qargi help environment.
  • qargi env check [--project P] [--repo DIR] [--timeout SECONDS] [--json] says whether a checkout is set up the way its project declares and ends with ENV OK or ENV INCOMPLETE: N missing (...) (exit 0, 1, or 2 for usage). It runs the doctor command once (no shell, standard input closed, a minimal environment, a time limit of 300 s by default), so it runs the project's code. A doctor line that begins with missing, fail, error, not ok, stale or [x], or ends with missing, not found or not installed, is a missing item; one that begins with expected or holds an env.known_failures entry is accepted. With no doctor command a built-in minimum runs (submodules, tags, pinned tools on PATH); for a stored project it adds whether skills, agents and memory are linked, STALE and DRIFT members, packs check and memory check. The verdict is recorded in state/env/PROJECT.json. A member may run it.
  • qargi env plan [--project P] [--repo DIR] --approve-exec NAME and qargi env apply --plan TOKEN --approved WORDS --approve-exec NAMES [--allow-root] (the lead's) look at, then run, a project's bootstrap. The plan runs the dry-run command (which can run project code, so it exits 2 without --approve-exec naming its executable), shows its output with privileged lines (sudo, doas, pkexec, su, run0) apart, and prints a token. Apply runs the dry run again, refuses when the token or the approved executables differ or when privileged lines are present without --allow-root, then runs the bootstrap on your terminal and ends with env check, so a bootstrap that leaves the environment incomplete exits 1. The member guard refuses both.
  • qargi project attach prints a development environment found: line and lists env gaps (no Development environment section in AGENTS.md or README.md, no bootstrap or doctor target). qargi project adopt writes a missing AGENTS.md and, when there is no task runner, a Makefile with stub targets; it never edits an existing file. qargi project new (the gitflow scaffold) writes the same AGENTS.md and Makefile stubs, and the scaffold's CLAUDE.md starts with @AGENTS.md. qargi provision plan prints the bootstrap command as a suggested setup script for the cloud environment. qargi help environment states the doctor line convention. This repository declares its own environment the same way (make -n bootstrap, make bootstrap, make doctor).
  • Release publishing: pushing a tag X.Y.Z runs .github/workflows/release.yml, which creates the GitHub release with the version's changelog section as notes and the source archive and its SHA-256 as files (a tag not on master, or an existing release, is left alone; it can be run by hand for an earlier tag). qargi release publish TAG does the same through gh (QARGI_GH) with a plan and token. release status|verify warn about a tag with no release and a commit without the workflow. lib/changelog_section.sh VERSION [FILE [HEADING]] prints a section.
  • Release signing is optional and off unless the project answers hold release.sign (key, namespace, files, optional verify_command). qargi release sign VERSION signs the listed files with ssh-keygen -Y sign on your own terminal (the passphrase never passes through qargi, a log or an agent; no ssh agent is asked), runs verify_command and records the result under state/release/. It runs only from the tag after finish and before publish, and is refused without a terminal, in a member run and under QARGI_NESTED. release publish attaches assets in the same call (--asset FILE, repeatable, and release.assets; --notes-file FILE or release.notes_file replaces the changelog notes) and, with release.sign set, refuses until a signature that still holds is recorded. release status says awaiting signature or VERSION is ready for signing: qargi release sign VERSION.
  • Release answers that fit a project's own layout, all optional and checked by project validate, init and set: release.version_file (default VERSION; none for a project with no version file), release.changelog.unreleased and release.changelog.released (heading templates with {version} and {date}), release.man_pages, release.test_command and release.preflight (a command, {version} replaced, run by release start and release push before they change anything). project attach and adopt read the changelog heading and version file by them.
  • Detached long-lived branches: the answer repo.detached lists branches (a documentation site, say) that never meet develop, master, release, hotfix or feature branches. qargi refuses every merge between them by name and by history. Tasks are cut from such a branch as from any base, and qargi feature merge BRANCH agent/SLUG with the detached branch as NAME merges a finished task into it (plan and token, local only).
  • Parking branch: the answer repo.parking_branch (default scratch) names the branch the main checkout rests on while qargi moves develop; a refusal because develop is checked out suggests git -C DIR switch -c scratch develop. qargi feature park [--project P] refreshes it (a dirty tree, or a parking branch with commits develop lacks, is refused). After feature finish and release finish a clean main checkout on the parking branch is fast-forwarded to develop. The parking branch is never pushed or merged.
  • Branch lifecycle answers: branches.push_features (never, when-shared, always; default never) decides whether feature start|merge|sync push the feature branch, and branches.delete_merged (local, local+remote; default local) decides whether feature finish also deletes it on origin (the plan shows it, and a branch with commits the feature lacks is kept).
  • Worktree root: the answer worktrees.root (default <state>/worktrees/PROJECT) is where qargi makes worktrees, at ROOT/<branch>. qargi feature start NAME --worktree creates ROOT/feature/NAME; feature merge|sync update a clean worktree of the feature, and feature finish removes it. feature list|status flag other worktrees of the project with the git worktree move that fixes it.
  • qargi branch prune [--project P] [--remote]: a plan and token for the merged agent/* and feature/* branches (with --remote also on origin, as a lease on the tip the plan showed) and the worktrees qargi made for them; --plan T --approved WORDS deletes them. A branch counts as merged only when it was merged with --no-ff; long-lived and detached branches, the parking branch, unmerged branches and branches checked out in a worktree qargi did not make are never touched, and each kept branch is listed with its reason. The member guard refuses it and feature park with sentences of their own.
  • lib/site.py, a documentation site generator (Python 3.11 or later, standard library only; python3 -I lib/site.py). build --release X.Y.Z --source DIR --out DIR [--pages DIR] [--url URL] writes a static site: a command reference generated from lib/commands.py (one page per command group, plus the help topics, files and environment variables), a releases page from CHANGELOG.md, the hand pages of --pages (Markdown with title and description front matter, converted by a strict subset converter that refuses what it does not support with the line number), sitemap.xml (dates from the last commit, never the build time), robots.txt, 404.html and .nojekyll. Each page has a title, description, canonical address, social-preview tags and structured data that describes only what the page shows; the stylesheet follows the reader's light or dark setting and needs no JavaScript. check validates the hand pages against the source (every qargi command and option they name exists in lib/commands.py, links and anchors resolve, the description is 120 to 155 characters), check-output DIR validates a built tree (well-formed HTML, unique ids, links, sitemap, no scripts, frames, forms or unsafe link schemes) and diff OLD NEW --source-old DIR --source-new DIR lists the commands, verbs and options that changed and the hand pages that still name what is gone. The build refuses paths outside the source tree, symbolic links, an --out that is not new or empty and a config or static/ folder other users can write; it reads the source's lib/commands.py in a boxed child process, so give it only a source you trust.
  • qargi release site VERSION regenerates the documentation site when a release ships: it builds the site of the tag VERSION with lib/site.py (the tag's tree is the source; the hand pages and site.json are those of the detached site branch) in a temporary worktree of that branch and commits it there as Site: built from release VERSION (site.json records the release, _site/ holds the built site), behind a plan token and an approval, touching no working tree. It never pushes and prints the git push command instead; a build error refuses with the generator's report. The answers are site.enabled, site.branch (default gh-pages when repo.detached lists it) and site.config (default site/site.json, the hand pages in pages/ beside it). With site.enabled, release finish ends with next: qargi release site VERSION (the new after_release step of the gitflow methodology, checked by methodology check and shown by methodology show) and release status says site: not built for VERSION, site: built at SHA, not pushed or site: pushed. The member guard refuses it.
  • qargi local list [--scratch DIR] lists the local runs the registry names, with role, slug, age, applied and merged. qargi local clean --applied --scratch DIR cleans every applied and merged run and keeps the rest (exit 1 when one was kept); local clean --stale DAYS --scratch DIR [--yes] lists finished runs older than DAYS and, with --yes, cleans each by the rules of clean RUN.
  • qargi provision plan|apply --force passes ant apply --force for a resource changed on the server; the token covers the flag.
  • Four baseline packs, each compatible_providers: ["any"]: review-findings, secrets-scan, docs-site-member and qargi-contributing. The qargi-providers skill ships with the others, and install.sh refuses a python3 older than 3.11.
  • python3 lib/help.py man --keep-date FILE keeps the .TH date of man/qargi.1, so regenerating the page after release start no longer undoes the date.
  • Tests: tests/test_skill_budget.sh holds every text a member or lead loads to an exact word ceiling (tests/skill-budget.txt; a ceiling raised above its value at the merge base needs a # raised: comment), forbids a 12-word sentence in two texts (tests/skill-dup-allowlist.txt), requires every qargi X Y example to name a real verb, and requires every reference file under skills/*/ to start with Load when ... and to be sent to ("load FILE") by its SKILL.md; a runtime's notes count as one text. tests/test_neutral.sh fails a vendor, model family or cloud CLI name in skills/, roles/, agents/, contract/, packs/skills/, provision/templates/*.md and methodologies/ beyond the counts in tests/vendor-words-allowlist.txt, which can only shrink. tests/test_tool_copy.sh keeps install.sh --copy's tool_dirs, the tests' TOOL_DIRS (one copy_tool helper in tests/hermetic.sh) and the top-level directories in step. tests/test_valued_opts.sh covers every option parser.
  • Numbered changelog items, opt-in with the answer release.changelog.numbered: true. Under the unreleased heading (release.changelog.unreleased, default ## [Unreleased]) an item is a line that starts N. or - N. ; the lines up to the next item belong to it. qargi changelog renumber [--project P] [--check] finds duplicate item numbers (two branches that each added an item 5), numbers the items again in file order from the first one's number and rewrites the (item N) cross-references (with a duplicated N, to the nearest item numbered N at or before the reference, else the nearest after it). It works on the CHANGELOG.md of the work tree around the current directory and leaves the change uncommitted; --check only reports and exits 1 on a duplicate. feature sync warns about duplicates after the merge, and feature finish refuses (exit 1, nothing changed) until they are renumbered, committed and verified. A member may run only --check; renumber without it is refused by the guard.
  • qargi upstream status|review|sync for a project that is a fork of an upstream repository and keeps its own changes, the overlay, on top of it. The answers name the remote (upstream.remote), the branch it follows (upstream.branch) and the local branch that carries the upstream line and nothing else (upstream.into, default upstream); upstream.overlay_check, optional, is a command array. status fetches that one branch of that remote (no tags, the only verb that reaches the network) and reports how far the branch is behind and ahead with the newest upstream commits; review [--limit N] lists the upstream commits not yet in the branch with the files each touches and marks the ones that touch a file develop changed since it parted from the upstream line; sync fast-forwards the branch to the fetched tip from a plan and a token (--plan, --approved), creates it at the tip when it does not exist, journals the move, refuses a branch with commits of its own, pushes nothing and never merges into develop (the next step, feature start upstream-X then feature merge, is printed); with upstream.overlay_check it then runs the command on a trial merge of the branch into develop in a temporary worktree (exit 1 on a failure or a conflict; the fast-forward stands). project validate checks the upstream answers. The guard refuses a member upstream status (its fetch changes the remote-tracking refs of the lead's repository, which local verify compares) and upstream sync, and project set of any upstream answer; review stays allowed. tests/test_upstream.sh runs the verbs against a local bare repository acting as upstream.
  • qargi ref record --rewrite REF OLD NEW --why "TEXT": the lead rewrites an agent/* branch to a commit with the same tree (git rev-parse OLD^{tree} must equal NEW's) while REF is at OLD, and the move is journaled with the reason, so local verify and local clean of a run prepared before it accept it and name it as a rewrite, and local clean and local list count the run's applied tip as merged when the commit it was rewritten to is. Refused to a member.
  • Local runs survive a reboot. local prepare warns on stderr when --scratch is on a tmpfs (a reboot loses the run; use a directory on disk). A passing local verify copies OUT, a run bundle beside it and the run's snapshots to <state>/runs/<run id>/; qargi review apply --from-saved ID applies from that copy with the same checks as a normal apply (review check, local verify --saved ID, the registry's repository, slug and base, applied once), and the guard keeps a member out of <state>/runs/. local list and qargi report show a run whose directory is gone as directory gone, with its saved copy; local clean RUN --discard drops the registry entry (and the saved copy) of such a run, and clean RUN does once its saved work is applied and merged. A clean marks the run cleaned in the registry and removes its saved copy.

Changed #

  • The CI workflow .github/workflows/test.yml (no scheduled run): a pull request into a branch other than master runs the fast tier and the steps its changed files cover, or the whole suite when it carries the label full-suite; a push to develop, a pull request into master (the release pull request) and a manual run run the whole suite in four shards, balanced by tests/durations.txt, and a last job, result, is red when any shard failed. A pull request replaces its own earlier run, a push to develop is never cancelled. Each job has a time limit computed from the manifest's budgets (35 minutes; the former 30 minutes for the whole suite in one job was less than the budgets add up to, and the job was cancelled), the packages jq and shellcheck come from a cache keyed by their list (.github/actions/tools), and every action is pinned to a full commit SHA.
  • tests/run.sh reads its steps from the manifest tests/suite.txt (tier, parallel-safe or serial, timeout, time budget, optional covers globs) and runs them -j N at a time (default: the CPUs, at most the cgroup quota; -j 1 is the former serial run). --tier fast runs a fast tier of about a minute that covers every area, --only PATTERN selects steps, --shard i/K deals them to K parts by recorded duration or budget, --shuffle SEED and --repeat N look for a test that fails now and then, and --enforce-budgets fails a step over 1.5 times its budget (otherwise a warning). Each step has its own session, HOME, no standard input and a timeout, and fails when it leaves a process running; its output is printed as one block when it ends, and the summary lists the failed steps and the slowest ten before the total: line. The linter runs through xargs -P. The runner fails when a tests/test_* file is not in the manifest or a listed file does not exist; tests/test_gitflow_detached.sh, which no list ran, is now listed. tests/test_runner.sh tests the runner.
  • tests/run.sh gives every step a TMPDIR of its own under the runner's directory, and compares the set of directories at the top level of the suite's TMPDIR before and after each step: a step that removed one it did not make, or left a new one, is named with the directories in its block (WARN directories outside its own changed: removed ..., left ...) and in a summary section. It is a warning, never a failure: with TMPDIR unset that place is /tmp, which every process on the host shares.
  • Every command starts faster: what bin/qargi does before a verb runs (the dev-run banner, the arguments filled in from the current directory, the project's cloud binding) is one python process, lib/help.py preamble, instead of three, and the model list behind the completion of a model value is read from the runtime descriptors only then, not on every start. qargi role list takes about half the time it did. tests/test_startup.py keeps the count at one process and the time under the shrink-only ceiling of tests/startup-budget.txt.
  • The tests are hermetic and safe to run concurrently with each other and with another whole suite: tests/hermetic.sh and tests/hermetic.py build one environment (fresh HOME, TMPDIR, config and state under one directory, UTC, C.UTF-8, umask 022, git without the host's configuration, no bytecode, no colour), and a lint (tests/hermetic_lint.py, run by tests/test_hermetic.sh) fails on a test that does not source it, names a literal /tmp, /dev/shm or /run path, kills by pattern, waits with a bare sleep, removes a directory it did not make, binds a fixed port, keeps a lock outside its directory or compares a wall-clock difference with a constant.
  • QARGI_WATCH_INTERVAL sets the poll interval of qargi watch in seconds (default 30), so a test of the watch runs in two seconds and not in a minute.
  • roles.ROLE.go is gone: a Go tool is a roles.ROLE.tools entry of kind go, and the cloud provision takes the environment's go packages from there (NAME@VERSION). project validate refuses the old key and says so. roles.ROLE.apt and .pip stay as they are: plain package lists of the cloud environment, with nothing pinned or hashed in them.
  • Breaking: nothing assumes Claude any more. Set a runtime per surface for every project (qargi project set P models.provider.local claude-code and models.provider.cloud claude-platform, or models.provider claude for the family). agent, provision, local prepare, local run, session starts, project validate, packs apply|check|link|unlink, skill accept and marshal handoff take the runtime from the project and exit 2 with set one with qargi project set P models.provider NAME when it is unset; a name that is not a project says no such project; --target must be the runtime's layout.render_target.
  • Breaking: members belong to a project. ~/.qargi/config/agents.json is {schema: 2, projects: {P: {NAME: record}}} and any other shape makes every agent verb exit 2 without touching the file (qargi upgrade warns): move it aside and add the members again with qargi agent add NAME --project P. --user is gone from agent add|refresh|rename and nothing is written to a runtime's user-level directory. Two projects can each have a worker. agent list shows PROJECT, NAME, ROLES, MODEL/EFFORT, FILE; agent remove NAME --project P is new; rename, refresh and remove take --project (else the project in effect, set by QARGI_PROJECT or the checkout) and act only on that project's member; agent models needs a project and says roles, not abilities, in --json. A member that an earlier agent refresh wrote into the checkout is not moved: remove it and add it again.
  • Breaking: the packs render lives in ~/.qargi/state/render/PROJECT/RUNTIME/ (it was state/claude/PROJECT; nothing converts the old directory: render again with qargi packs apply --target RUNTIME PROJECT, then qargi packs link PROJECT so a session in the checkout loads it, and remove the old directory by hand). lib/packs_render.py takes the skills directory, MCP file and settings from the runtime's definition. The link engine behind packs link handles a directory link, one link per entry, or a copy.
  • Breaking: library skill and tool packs need compatible_providers: qargi skill seal NAME --compatible any (or a list); packs seed declares it on the baseline packs. Skill content hashes are stricter (symlinks, the executable bit and nested files count), so an accepted skill shows drifted once: qargi skill accept it again. Members show STALE until qargi agent refresh NAME, and cloud agents' prompts are stale: qargi instances refresh-prompt NAME --if-stale.
  • Breaking: a usage error exits 2, as the manual page says (an unknown option, a usage line, a missing NAME, RUN or project, options that need each other); it was 1 in every shell verb and in discover, export, import and methodology. A refusal that depends on state or on an approval is still exit 1. A valued option given as the last word (qargi agent for build --surface, upgrade --branch, project new --dir) now ends with exit 2 and OPT needs a value.
  • Breaking: the marshal lease length is the project answer marshal.lease_minutes (it was marshal.ttl; set the new key and drop the old one), a whole number of minutes from 1 to 1440, default 15. project set and project validate refuse any other value.
  • Breaking: feature finish no longer deletes the feature branch on origin by default (it did whenever a tracking ref existed). Set branches.delete_merged to local+remote for that.
  • Breaking: models.extensions and models.accept_no_barrier change only through provider enable|disable and provider accept. project set refuses them with exit 2 (it was 1), and project init|attach|new and qargi import refuse a file that adds or changes an entry (dropping one is allowed; restore a project by project init, then provider enable).
  • Breaking: install.sh --uninstall removes exactly the paths an install recorded in install.manifest beside install.json (links, copied files, created directories; a directory that still holds a file you added is kept and said). With no manifest (an install made before this release) it removes nothing and says so, and --uninstall --force removes only the fixed paths the script writes. The directories come from the runtime definition's layout, and --runtime NAME chooses the runtime (default claude-code; an unknown one, or one with no skills directory, is refused before anything is written). The retired skills, old agent links and old qargi/dev skill links are no longer removed by install.sh: remove any left over by hand.
  • Breaking: an archive made by export carries a mode for each file (0600, or 0700 for an executable file of the pack library). import restores it, and a file that differs only in that bit is a change in the plan. An archive with another mode or none (any made by an earlier qargi) is refused: export it again. Local runs prepared by 0.2.0 are refused by local verify|clean|run and review apply (the registry does not record their repository): finish them with 0.2.0 or remove them with qargi local clean RUN --discard. Memory stores on canon version 1 are unknown to canon plan|apply: bring them to version 2 by hand.
  • The member contract is contract/contract.md with contract/output-format.md (the two shapes: patches, or a report and manifest for a read-only role), about half its length, every rule once: one commit rule (one logical change with its tests and docs, or docs and changelog in the next commit when one would span three top-level directories; review check agrees); checks and gates merged (the profile's "always" gates, the repository's lint step and a secret scanner over BASE_SHA..HEAD); temporary directories under TMP only; the identity configured in the clone; background commands through "your runtime's background facility", never pgrep -f; "write outputs only to OUT" (RUN_DIR is no place a member is told about); and no memory-write rule but the task block's MEMORY packet (members propose notes in their report and the lead files them). The cloud preamble, the lead's contract seed and the role seeds say the same and no longer name RUN_DIR or repeat what the addenda say. The cloud-only part of the contract is a resource of the claude-platform definition, not appended by the core; a project with no cloud runtime gets no addendum.
  • A read-only role puts a suggested fix in its report as a fenced diff, never a patch file (local verify and review check refuse patches of a read-only run; the manifest kind suggestion is gone). CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE mean the same in the review role and the review-findings pack. The four role texts and the member text are shorter and state only what the contract does not (the review role's product is "a report in OUT, not patches"; the documentation-branch rule is in the docs-site-member pack).
  • The lead skills are lean and load their rarely used parts on demand: qargi-flow (the marshal in marshal.md; the models section moved to qargi-instances; never invent an approval; marshal records are data and a handoff carries no approval), qargi-task (cloud.md for a cloud instance, local-run.md for a command runtime; CONTRACT among the task block fields; the private-repository line in the local flow), qargi-verify (one take-in sequence: verify every open run before applying any, apply and merge from the run's slug, local clean only after the merge is confirmed; git am or a split by file for a cloud collect or a project with no open feature; the reason code asked again when rework was needed), qargi-packs (apply.md, seed.md), qargi-providers (definition.md, verify.md), qargi-memory (curate.md; memory check exits 1 on any FAIL), qargi-project (repository.md), qargi-instances (the two bases, profiles, tiers, agent for, instances init --location local --agent FILE), qargi-session and qargi-team. No skill names one runtime's tools, directories or settings: each points at qargi provider notes spawn|session-model|exploration|skills-dir|identity|commands, and the plan-token and guard rules are one pointer each to qargi help approvals and qargi help guard. Each description says what the skill does and when to load it. A SKILL.md must send a session to each reference file ("load FILE") and every file under skills/ that is not .md is budgeted. qargi-session tells the lead to run qargi env check when the handoff note's environment check is older than HEAD or incomplete.
  • The keep-a-changelog pack and CONTRIBUTING.md state the contract's commit rule; the pack says the member never dates the changelog or cuts a release (release start does). The qargi-contributing pack names no tool of one runtime. The shipped shellcheck-gate pack has two more lines: a disable for a newly introduced shellcheck code names the version that introduced it, and a lint severity the project configures itself beats -S warning (packs seed offers the update).
  • qargi local prepare gives the run its own copy of the contract and prints CONTRACT= in the first, eval-able block and in the TASK-BLOCK PATHS block; it records a relative --repo and --scratch as real paths and tmpdir in the registry. Its help lists every key it prints.
  • qargi team brief and qargi collect read the hosted output and clone directories from the cloud runtime's notes (output-dir, clone-dir); a brief for a project with no cloud runtime is refused. collect finds the project from the session's instance.
  • provider check is no longer on the member guard's read-only list (it records a result); provider model and provider notes|addenda are allowed to a member (they only print). provider check runs adapters with a fixed environment.
  • The member guard reads the text of a quoted argument or heredoc body as data when every command of the line is echo, cat, tee, grep or git commit|log|status|diff|show|add, so a commit message that mentions a refused verb is no longer refused. Any other program, a comment, a backslash, a substitution, $'..', ${..}, an unclosed quote or an assignment keeps the plain split, and git push, gh and ssh in text are refused as before. Under the read-only class a Bash command may write OUT and the run's temporary directory, as the Write tool does, and git tag with no argument or with -l/--list lists tags.
  • qargi project set P deployment VALUE says only what was set for a methodology option. skill import prints note: the source's top-level .pack.json ... when the source holds a record of its own.
  • Help and manual wording: agent, concepts and roles speak of roles, not abilities; provider describes one runtime on one surface; local run, local prepare and the render warning name no vendor and say --target RUNTIME; local run lists its exit statuses 0 to 4 and review check its exit 1; a refusal of the read-only class says "under the read-only class"; the manual page's SEE ALSO lists every shipped skill (a copy without skills/ names them generically). qargi help guard names every verb the guard refuses, the protected files and directories (the pack library, credentials, install.json, state/render, the memory tiers, the state's providers/, the ref journal and the run registry, the marshal and feature directories, the runtimes' skills, agents and plugin directories, the lead's git configuration and session files), the rules for cd, the 5-second budget and the git commit -F FILE advice, within 330 words; tests/test_help.py fails when a refused verb is in neither the topic nor a documented exemption, and compares the manual page's APPROVALS and GUARD sections with the topics.
  • qargi feature finish NAME refuses a feature that is behind develop when both sides changed the same files since their merge base (exit 1, nothing changed). It lists those files and says to run qargi feature sync NAME first. A feature behind develop with no file in common is refused as before, without the list.
  • qargi release status VERSION shows, next to the full-suite verdict, the command that produced it and when it ran (from the suite record). When release.test_command is set and is not that command, or the project's test_command changed since the run, a line of its own says so, so the pass is not read as the release gate. A record made by another command is shown, not reported as "not run".
  • qargi release start VERSION lists, after it creates the branch, the features merged into develop since the previous tag (the --no-ff merges whose message is "Merge branch 'feature/...'"), one per line with the short sha, or says there are none.
  • local verify and local clean accept qargi's own moves and name them (develop moved by qargi feature finish), so a run no longer has to be cleaned before the next feature finish. The ref journal also records the pushes, the deletions on origin and the tags of feature finish, release finish (and hotfix), release push, branch prune --remote and the pushes of branches.push_features (lines with remote: "origin" and the origin URL); verify accepts a remote-tracking ref of origin that says what origin has (a fetch), a tag fetched from origin, the parking branch fast-forwarded to develop's tip (by hand too), and every journaled move after a passing verify as well as before (a journaled deletion failed there).

Removed #

  • Schema 1 provider definitions (lib/providers/claude.json, schema.json, the claude/adapter router) and all schema-1 code. claude is a family, not a runtime (unknown provider 'claude' from the verbs that take a runtime name). project template reads no Claude file: roles carry model: null until a runtime is set.
  • qargi migrate (roles and home), the refusal that told you to run it, the import of archives made with the old role names, and lib/roles.py; the guard no longer protects ~/.config/qargi.
  • qargi canon import (--map docs-v0), the imports list of canon/layout.json and the canon section that described it: move the notes of such a store into the layout by hand. Canon chains older than version 2 (canon plan|apply --default-role, provision/canon-seed/v1/, tests/canon_sim.py); setting up an empty store has its own step.
  • qargi review prune [--yes] (use qargi branch prune, which shows a plan and a token, also clears merged feature/* branches and the worktrees qargi made, and checks that a branch was merged with --no-ff; review prune deleted any agent/* branch that was an ancestor of develop or a feature).
  • agent add --abilities (use --roles), local prepare --ability (use --role) and the ABILITY= line of local prepare.
  • The one-per-role fallback: agent for ROLE resolves only the project's worker or reviewer (exit 1 with the agent add command when the base is missing; --json has no legacy; agent models says not a base), on the cloud surface too (agent for ROLE --surface cloud --project P prints the base or refuses: exit 1 unregistered, exit 2 overrides not verified). An instance of one role still works by name (qargi send <project>-build ...).
  • The judgement of a local run made before RUN/class and RUN/started existed: no class counts as read-only, no started has no ref-journal entry and no age (local list shows ?, --stale names it as skipped).
  • qargi credential askpass FILE (internal, nothing called it) and the unreachable second version) branch of bin/qargi.
  • From the role texts and the contract: the paragraphs that repeated the contract, the "Before DONE" tail, the build role's "Return numbered patches" line, the review role's enforcement note, the PDF-skill sentence and the memory-store bullets.

Fixed #

  • The memory packet local prepare prints keeps to its cap of 3000 characters also when it ends with the line that says rows were left out (it could exceed it by up to 33 characters, more or fewer depending on the paths in the rows).
  • The memory packet local prepare prints keeps to its cap of 3000 characters also when it ends with the line that says rows were left out (it could exceed it by up to 33 characters, more or fewer depending on the paths in the rows).
  • marshal status, marshal handoff and feature status list an unmerged agent branch only under the feature its run was prepared against (local prepare --base feature/NAME, the base the registry of local runs records), not under every feature; the agent branches of no open feature are said once, on one unattributed agent branches line. The handoff note lists only the agent branches merged since the feature was cut from develop, not every merged branch in the history (the (and 51 more) tail).
  • Task lines tell the truth: marshal status, marshal handoff and feature status said not verified of a run that had passed local verify, been applied, merged and cleaned. A passing local verify marks the run's line in the registry of local runs verified and local clean marks it cleaned (the line stays, one per run, rewritten under the registry's lock); a task reads verified, applied or not verified as the registry and the run directory say, and a cleaned run is listed only on a cleaned: line, never as an open task. feature merge of an agent branch whose run exists and has no passing verify warns.
  • packs check --target T PROJECT no longer reports manifest missing for a project that was never applied, which looked like a broken render. It prints not applied: ... (qargi packs apply ...) and exits 0, and a render directory without its manifest still fails. The answer packs.none: true (qargi project set P packs.none true; project set of packs is refused to a member) says the project uses no project packs: the check passes with no render, and fails when a pack is linked to a role of the project. The section of the skills a session would load, the unmanaged ones in ~/.claude/skills included, is printed in every case.
  • qargi project set P PATH false stored the string false; it stores the JSON value, like true and numbers.
  • local clean --stale DAYS --scratch DIR reported 0 runs when the run directories were gone (a reboot that emptied a tmpfs): it now plans and, with --yes, drops the records of such runs older than DAYS, keeping the one whose saved copy holds work that was never applied; a scratch directory that is gone itself is still read from the registry (local list --scratch too).
  • agent verbs check the records of the project they are about, not every project; agent rename keeps a member file edited by hand and says so; a record that lacks roles or file is refused with one line naming the member.
  • The dispatcher finds the project of an instance PROJECT-ROLE for every role, not only the four built-in ones and lead.
  • The git authentication helper is a fixed script, lib/askpass.sh, reading the file in QARGI_ASKPASS_FILE; it left a qargi-askpass.* file in the temporary directory on every call.
  • qargi release: finish names the repository without .git and reaches GitHub only through $QARGI_GH; start refuses a version whose tag exists; the pull request is titled PROJECT VERSION; publish shares the one exit handler. release start always sets the date and version of every manual page (an empty .TH date is filled) and release finish refuses a page that lost them, and, when release.version_file is none, a changelog with no section for the version.
  • qargi review check OUT reads the patches from OUT/patches/*.patch only (it also took OUT/*.patch, which review apply never read), accepts a read-only run's report under an OUT_PREFIX, says OUT where it said RUN_DIR, and refuses an unknown option or a second directory with exit 2. review apply takes the patch files as a list (a space in a name is one patch) and finds the run by its real path. The qargi-verify skill and the README say review check takes the output directory.
  • qargi local clean: refuses a run whose commits were never applied or whose applied branch is merged into no branch but agent/* (--discard drops them on purpose and says how many); --discard also removes a run whose refs changed (verify's outcome is a warning). It removes the temporary directory the lead's registry names for the run (only a real path directly under /dev/shm, QARGI_RUN_TMP or the run, never through a link or a trailing slash; a run prepared before this has none, so its directory is left), and only RUN/tmp when the registry has no line. local list|clean check the second word of applied before giving it to git, and local list prints the role, slug and path without control bytes. local run takes TMPDIR from the registry too. local verify and local clean no longer refuse the move that feature merge DETACHED BRANCH made to a detached branch.
  • qargi memory check reports a half-initialised tier as INFO ... (qargi memory init NAME finishes it) instead of asking you to correct the path; an interrupted set-up of a store or tier can be finished by running it again.
  • export and import can move a project between hosts: a name in an archive may begin with a dot (so the library's .pack.json records pass; . and .. do not), a memory note's name is checked with the same rule as every other name, export checks every name before it writes and stops, naming the file and how to go on (rename it, or --only), and says when it leaves out a symbolic link or a note whose name the reader would refuse. A script in a skill keeps its executable bit.
  • Importing a pack directory that carries qargi's own record follows one rule shared by import, review, content hash, render and audit: the top-level .pack.json is qargi's metadata and is ignored and not copied; a deeper one is skill content, so the review fails it and the hash counts it.
  • install.sh --user --copy copied the tool without canon/ and catalog/; it copies from one list (tool_dirs), and tests/test_install.sh runs qargi help and qargi discover search from the copy.
  • A cloud agent's prompt and local prepare stop with the reason when the project's runtime is set but does not resolve, instead of leaving the addenda out; instances refresh-prompt records no hash for a prompt that failed to render, so instances show says unknown. No project, a project not stored, or no runtime for the surface still means no addendum.
  • packs check --target claude-code no longer reports "shadowing" for every rendered skill once the checkout's skills directory is the link made by packs link. packs link|unlink work through no-follow descriptors and say where your skills are when something fails; names in offers are quoted and control characters stripped; an unusual name is skipped: unusual name.
  • The member guard no longer refuses valid work: a file write because one provider definition in the library is broken (it skips it with one note); qargi provider model; tee OUT/report.md < r.md; $OUT and ${OUT} in a write (they mean RUN/out unless the command could give OUT a value); git commit -m push, git log -S push, git grep push and git branch push (it looks only at the git subcommand); a copy into the home directory (cp src/a.go ~/, rsync -a build/ ~/, grep -r TODO ~, find ~), which is no read of the signing key (copying or searching the credentials directory itself still is); an mv into a directory that only lies above a protected place; a trimming expansion such as ${f%%:*}; the script of sed -i -e, sed -i -f and perl -pi -e; cd ../../out && echo "$(date)" > report.md; and a build member editing the repository's own docs/tmpdir. A directory of the clone that holds a file named like the run's record is not taken for the run. Its tool names are the member's matcher's (MultiEdit and NotebookRead are gone from the hook data and the shipped definition).
  • The member guard stays within the hook's time: a command it cannot check within 5 seconds is refused (a killed hook does not block), and two quadratic regular expressions (a long run of blanks; many marshal handoff or project set words) are gone. A brace expression is expanded whole or the call is refused (more than 256 words for one word or 20000 for the command).
  • The guard's refusals to a read-only member say the report goes to OUT (they said RUN_DIR), and the refusal of a skill change says to propose it in the report.
  • qargi env check printed packs: no drift for a project whose packs were never applied, since packs check passes then; it prints packs: not applied (qargi packs apply --target T PROJECT), a note and not a missing item.
  • qargi env check counted a STALE, DRIFT or MISSING member as current when the path of its file made the agent list line longer than 160 characters: the line was cut before its state was read.
  • install.sh --project DIR --uninstall (and --user --uninstall) left an empty ~/.qargi/config behind. The install records the config directory and the parents it had to create, and the uninstall removes them once nothing else is left in them.

Security #

  • A member's qargi project set of roles.ROLE.tools (or of a whole role, or of roles) is refused, as env.*, release.* and test_command are: the list names what env apply installs and runs with the lead's rights and what local prepare checks out.
  • The member guard refuses more of what runs a refused verb or git push, and allows nothing the earlier guard refused:
    • It cuts a Bash command at every ;, &&, ||, |, & and newline, inside quotes, comments and heredocs too (write a commit message to a file and git commit -F FILE), reads a command substitution as a command of its own wherever it sits, a verb after then, do, !, (, {, a case pattern, a redirection or a function definition, git push and gh inside sh -c, $'...' and $"..." quoting as the plain string, a subcommand or verb that a variable or substitution builds, and the command after find -exec or in parallel's operands. It refuses git send-pack, http-push, svn dcommit, an rsync operand of the form host:path, git -c with an alias or program key, --config-env, --exec-path and the GIT_CONFIG_*, GIT_EXEC_PATH and GIT_SSH_COMMAND variables.
    • A command with a NUL byte, over 262144 characters, nested more than 40 substitutions deep, with a glob that needs more than 4000 directory entries, with more than 24 directories at once, or taking over 5 seconds to check is refused, because a hook killed at its timeout does not block.
    • Redirections before the program or standing alone, >|, <>, >&FILE, git log|diff|show --output, format-patch -o, archive -o, bundle create, sort -o, uniq IN OUT, cp|mv|install|ln -t, dd of=, sed -i, tee, tar, unzip, curl, wget, patch, git apply --directory, git clone|init|worktree add DIR, awk -i inplace, ex|vi|vim|nvim|ed, rename, sqlite3, setfacl, mkfifo, find -delete|-exec rm, ln of a protected location, and the git subcommands that write objects or the index are writes to their target; the Edit and Write tools are held to the same. A target built by a glob, a variable or a substitution is refused when it could be a file of the run's record or hide it, as is a file name with a ;, |, & or newline that leads into a protected location.
    • A cd is followed only when it surely happens (a plain top-level command, or a chain of cds after &&); otherwise the commands after it are judged from every directory the shell may be in. After a cd it cannot read (cd "$d", env -C, CDPATH) a relative write is refused until an absolute cd. git --work-tree=DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE count like -C DIR. ${NAME...} forms are read by the environment's value.
    • A line with printf -v (and read or local) is no longer read as text only, since it assigns a variable; a heredoc delimiter that starts with # is left to the plain split.
    • The run's record (ability, class, profile, refs.before, refs.before.new, applied, repo.path, repo.url, cred.path, dispatch.json, task.md, tmpdir, started, verified, refs.after, refs.diff, git) cannot be written, moved, removed, copied, linked or truncated, nor the run directory itself used as a destination (cp -r Y/. ../.., tar -C ../.. -xf, unzip -d ../..); notes, out/, clone/ and tmp/ stay writable. The read-only class holds when its hook passes --class read-only even if ability and refs.before were moved away, and refuses git bisect, symbolic-ref with a value, reflog expire|delete, hash-object -w, unpack-objects, git lfs writes, a git tag that makes, replaces or deletes a tag (options read as git reads them, abbreviations included) and setting PATH, GIT_*, PAGER, BASH_ENV, RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH, LD_*.
    • For every member: the lead's git configuration (~/.gitconfig, ~/.config/git, git config --global|--system|--file outside the clone, git init of the home directory), session settings and startup files (~/.claude/settings.json, settings.local.json, CLAUDE.md, commands/, hooks/, ~/.claude.json, ~/.bashrc and the other shell startup files, ~/.ssh/config, authorized_keys), the run registry and its lock, the lead's run and agent verbs (local prepare|verify| clean, agent remove, project new, team run, task, also through local.sh, agent.sh, team.sh), project set|init| link|unlink whenever its words cannot be read statically, provider check and provider adapter-run, and the link and render scripts of the tool itself. Every read of the signing key is refused, also through a leading or numbered redirection (<KEY cat, exec 3<KEY), and mv -T into a protected place is too.
  • local verify|clean|run, local list, review apply and clean --applied|--stale act only on runs the lead's registry (state/local-runs.jsonl) names, and take the run's repository (repo, or url and cred, the path of the credential file and never a token), slug, base and temporary directory from it, not from files in the run directory that a member can write. A repository a member chose ran its own .git/config in the lead's shell, and a repo.url with a cred.path sent any readable file as a token to a host of the member's choice. A run whose files differ from the registry is refused with the difference named; a run the registry does not name, or names with no repository, is refused too, and clean --discard still removes it. local list reads started as a number and prints ? for anything else (the text was used in shell arithmetic).
  • qargi local run writes OUT/transcript, OUT/transcript.err and RUN/dispatch.json only as a new or a regular file with no second name, opened without following a link or waiting for a reader, and checks dispatch.json before it starts the process; OUT must be a directory of the run. It reads RUN/task.md, profile and ability the same way, and a run with no ability is refused with a message. qargi review apply writes the run's applied record and refs.before snapshot in the lead's state directory and renames them into the run (mv -T), and an applied that is a link or not a plain file refuses the apply.
  • A runtime's adapter (provider adapter-run, so agent for --surface cloud and the session verbs) ran with the caller's whole environment, forge tokens and ssh agent included. It gets the small environment a pack gets plus dispatch.env_pass, which also refuses HOME, PATH, LD_*, GH_*, SSH_*, JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS, FPATH, ZDOTDIR, KSH_ENV, LUA_*, LESSOPEN, GLIBC_TUNABLES, NPM_CONFIG_*, GOFLAGS, GOENV, INPUTRC, TERMINFO and SUDO_ASKPASS. A member's command also gets LC_ALL and TZ.
  • A library provider pack with no record (placed by hand) is not loaded, run, checked or attested: seal or import it. Skill and tool packs are held to the text-only policy of provider packs (no binaries, archives, links, special files or file over 1 MB; scripts stay allowed and listed); the review refuses control and bidi characters, also as JSON escapes, and prints everything escaped. The content hash of a skill pack also covers a link, a pipe, a socket, an empty directory and a file with a second name; a pack without any of them hashes as before, so no approval is lost.
  • A runtime that claims read_only_barrier with barrier kind none and no read-only arguments fails provider check and import and reads as no barrier, as does a barrier hook whose refusal cannot be told from an allow (equal exit codes, or an empty stdout object); a local run of a read-only member is refused for it unless the project ran provider accept.
  • qargi local prepare refuses a --repo-url that carries a user name or a password; the token goes in --credential-file.
  • qargi project link (memory) compares real paths, so a link below the memory root that leads outside it is refused, and a project whose tiers resolve without a project tier is refused with a message, not a traceback.
  • qargi project set of release.*, test_command, env.* or site.* is refused to a member, as models.* is: the lead later runs those commands, or builds and commits the documentation site from site.* (qargi release site), so a member that set them would run its own command with the lead's rights.
  • The member guard refuses git config that writes a key which makes git run a program, read another configuration file or give a command or a remote another name, as it refused the one-shot git -c form: git config core.fsmonitor ..., git config alias.x '!...', git config include.path ..., git config core.hooksPath ... and git config alias.p push (then git p pushed) were allowed since 0.2.0. Both forms share one list (core.fsmonitor, hooksPath, sshCommand, editor, pager, askPass, gitProxy, include.path, includeIf.*.path, alias.*, filter, diff, merge and tool drivers, credential, sequence.editor, gpg, uploadpack, receivepack, remote.*.url|pushurl|uploadpack|receivepack, url.*.insteadOf, submodule.*.update, protocol.ext.allow), read in any case, in every scope and file, after -C, in the git config set syntax; --edit, a renamed section and a key that a variable or xargs brings are refused too. user.name, user.email and the other plain settings stay allowed, and GIT_CONFIG=FILE in front of git config names the file it writes, so a protected one is refused.
  • On a line that also runs git, the member guard also refuses a write under .git/modules/, .git/worktrees/ or to a config.worktree (the configuration and hooks of a submodule or a worktree), as it did for .git/config and .git/hooks.
  • The member guard reads the program a shell takes from its standard input: echo "qargi upgrade" | bash, bash <<< "qargi upgrade", sh -s <<< ..., . /dev/stdin <<< ..., echo ... | source /dev/stdin, echo ... | xargs -0 sh -c, printf '%s' ... | bash and echo ... > f; sh f ran the verb unseen since 0.2.0. The text the line shows (a here-string, an echo or printf piped in or written to the file the shell runs) is now read as sh -c text is, and a program it cannot see (cat file | bash, curl ... | sh, bash < file, a process substitution, a file cp writes in the same command) is refused: write the script with the file tool and run bash FILE.
  • The member guard finds the lead identity QARGI_LEAD among the names a command sets the way it finds QARGI_NESTED: printf -vQARGI_LEAD x (the name glued to -v), mapfile and readarray into it, and env -uQARGI_LEAD were not refused.

0.2.0 #

Released 2026-11-02. The GitHub release

Added #

  • qargi marshal forget NAME: drops this machine's accepted marshal mark of one feature, so a stale mark (left after the feature was deleted or re-created on the remote) stops reporting rollback detected. It needs integrity advisory or strict and a mark for NAME, prints the mark's revision and commit in a plan whose token covers both, applies with --plan and your words (audited as marshal:forget), touches no other feature and nothing on the remote, and is refused in a member run.
  • qargi project adopt PROJECT: closes the safe gaps of an attached repository. With a plan token and your words it creates the missing long-lived branches locally (at the default branch tip; none is moved) and writes the methodology files that do not exist as one commit on agent/adopt-<methodology> cut from develop, for you to review. It never overwrites a file, never pushes, leaves the working tree alone, refuses a dirty tree, a detached HEAD and a member run, and lists the changelog format, tag format and CI content as left for you.
  • Signed marshal records. With the shared marshal, each lead machine can have its own ssh key (marshal key init), a per-project signers file lists the trusted keys (marshal signers add|remove|list, never in the repository or the refs), and marshal enable --integrity off|advisory|strict sets the mode. Records are signed with ssh-keygen -Y (namespace qargi-marshal) over a canonical payload that names project, feature, kind, revision, parent and lead, so a record cannot be altered or moved to another feature. Advisory tags records signed, unsigned or INVALID; strict ignores unsigned and invalid ones and falls back to the last accepted record. A local high-water mark detects a rewound ref (rollback detected), and junk or replayed pushes neither renew a lease nor block a feature. marshal resign NAME signs an existing record when moving from advisory to strict. Keys, signers and the mode are yours to set; nothing is signed until you choose a mode. Members cannot read the signing key or change the signers. Review hardening: a lagging machine builds on the newest signed record rather than overwriting it; advisory builds on an unsigned head instead of dropping it; a signed finish records the last features commit so a reused name keeps its rollback mark; records are identified by what the signature covers, so a re-committed head is the same record; resign shows the head, lead and goal in a plan whose token covers that head and refuses a lead other than the accepted one; disable needs the plan token and your words while integrity is on; the guard follows pushd/popd, refuses links and moves of the key, and normalises /./ in scanned text. Member definitions now also hook the guard on the Read and Grep tools (to keep the key unread); members created earlier keep the old matcher until they are refreshed (qargi agent refresh NAME).
  • Shared marshal. qargi marshal enable|disable switch a project between the local records and a shared backend that keeps each feature record as a commit on refs/qargi/features/NAME of the remote origin: create-only claims, leased updates, an atomic move to refs/qargi/done/NAME on finish, a fetch that never brings other refs, and takeover judged on the taker's own monotonic clock. It is off by default, needs the plan token and your typed words, is audited, cannot be used from a member run, and project set refuses marshal.* except marshal.ttl. Offline verbs use the cache and say remote not checked; an offline claim is provisional. local verify ignores refs/qargi/; marshal status|check take --no-fetch (the session hook uses it). Hardening from review: an offline claim is dropped, not pushed, when another machine finished the feature meanwhile; remote records with wrong field types are ignored instead of crashing readers; takeover of a provisional claim is refused; the lease renewer survives an unreachable remote (exit status 3, remote not checked) and stops only on a lost lease; the fetch leaves FETCH_HEAD alone (git 2.29+); marshal ignores APPROVED and PLAN_ARG from the environment; and qargi feature start|finish|verify are refused to a member.
  • Cloud profiles. A project can provision two cloud base agents, <project>-worker (write class) and <project>-reviewer (read-only), and start a session of a role and profile on one: qargi start|send <project>-worker --role build --profile build. The model and effort are overridden per session with a full model object and the role's prompt is rendered fresh, so the base needs no prompt refresh; its tools stay fixed on the agent. agent for ROLE --surface cloud resolves the instance and uses a base only when it is registered and the provider's cloud override capabilities are verified (they now are for claude, from a scratch run on 2026-11-01); otherwise the four role agents keep serving, and a profile with a different model than the role agent refuses. A reviewer base needs the project's provider accept for the missing cloud read-only barrier before it is provisioned or started. The claude adapter gained a start-session request builder, with a conformance check that a body never carries tools, skills or MCP servers.
  • Providers. Each model provider is a descriptor (lib/providers/NAME.json, one schema) with its tier-to-model map and verification dates, effort levels, surfaces and a per-surface capability matrix; qargi provider list|show|check prints and validates them, and check says what degrades (an unverified capability counts as unsupported). The claude provider has a local adapter (lib/providers/claude/adapter: resolve, dispatch-local, barrier-check) behind which members are rendered, and the Claude model ids and id pattern that were spread through the code now come from its descriptor. A surface with no read-only barrier cannot serve the review role unless the project records models.accept_no_barrier with qargi provider accept (plan and token, audit-logged); for claude that means a cloud review role needs your acceptance, while the local guard counts as a partial barrier. A provider with no effort control has the effort dropped and agent models says so, agent for refuses a profile on a provider that cannot override the model per dispatch, and local verify and review apply never apply patches from a read-only run. bash tests/conformance.sh NAME runs a conformance suite (verb shapes, unsupported verbs, secrets out of argv, a barrier corpus, the read-only definition) against an adapter, with a deliberately broken adapter proving the suite catches faults. A member cannot run provider accept.
  • Base members and profiles. Two base members, one per guard class: worker (build, write, test) and reviewer (review, read-only); qargi agent add worker|reviewer defaults to the base's own abilities and refuses abilities of the other class. Specializations are profiles {base, tier, effort, purpose}, resolved at dispatch: shipped build, write, test, review, auditor (Haiku), advisor (Opus) and the opt-in researcher (frontier tier), plus your own under profiles.NAME in a project's answers (validated; a profile whose abilities do not fit its base's class is refused). qargi agent for ROLE [--profile NAME] [--json] now prints one line, MEMBER MODEL EFFORT PROFILE, and the lead passes the model and the effort to the Agent tool, which override the member definition. qargi local prepare --profile NAME resolves the profile before any clone, records it in RUN/profile (a file the guard keeps from the member) and prints PROFILE, MEMBER, MODEL and EFFORT. The tier-to-model table lives in the provider file (lib/providers/claude.json, with an alias per tier for local dispatch). qargi agent models flags legacy per-ability members, a missing base, refused profiles and mixed-class members. The earlier model-table entry is superseded: roles and suggested became profiles, and auditor, advisor and researcher are profiles, not members.
  • Model selection. One table (lib/model-defaults.json) names a tier and an effort for the lead and each role (Sonnet 5.5 for the lead, build, write and test, Opus 5.5 for review), and lib/providers/claude.json maps the tiers (fast, balanced, deep, frontier) to models; a project chooses the provider with models.provider. qargi agent add takes its model and effort from the project's answers, else the table, and writes the effort into the member definition (so does agent refresh); the project template does the same, and its write role is now Sonnet rather than Opus. qargi agent models [--project P] [--json] shows the table, the project's overrides, the shipped profiles (auditor on Haiku, advisor on Opus, researcher on the opt-in frontier tier, Fable 5.1) and each member, marking an alias as unpinned and a frontier member as opt-in. The flow skill has an advisor sign-off before feature finish and says search is a read-only exploration on a small model, not a role.
  • qargi marshal status --all (and --brief, --json, and the session-start hook that uses them) lists only the open features; --history adds the finished and abandoned records after them. qargi marshal check NAME for a name that has no branch and no record now exits 1 with no feature NAME, and so do the flow verbs and local prepare --base feature/NAME for such a name. The error for a branch that is checked out elsewhere says how to free it (git -C DIR checkout --detach).
  • Memory tiers (writing, second slice). The session-start hook now lists the notes of the tiers, highest first, as data after the marshal block (at most 4000 characters per note and 16000 in all; a tier that is missing or unreadable is skipped and named). qargi memory init TIER creates a tier from the standard layout and qargi memory move PATH --from TIER --to TIER moves a note, or a folder of notes, between tiers; both print a plan and a token and apply only with your approval, and nothing is synced or deleted without it. A repo tier with notes that are not committed warns with the count. local prepare prints a TASK-BLOCK MEMORY packet for the member, and the guard refuses a member every verb and script that writes a tier. The memory, task and canon documents describe the tiers.
  • Baseline packs. qargi ships three packs under packs/: shellcheck-gate (lint every shell file you touch and quote the verdict), keep-a-changelog (one Unreleased entry per user-visible change, in the same commit) and gitflow-member (a member's part of a git-flow project). qargi packs seed stores them in your library: it prints one line per pack (add, update, current or kept) and a plan token, and applies with your approval; an untouched shipped copy is updated when qargi ships newer text, a copy you edited and sealed or a pack of your own with the same name is kept and never overwritten, and seeding never links a pack. install.sh (and so qargi upgrade) adds the packs your library lacks with packs seed --install, which needs no token and never updates. Link a pack to a project with qargi skill link; proposing links when a project is created or attached is not built yet. A member cannot run packs seed.
  • Memory tiers (read-only, first slice). A project's memory is five ranked tiers, highest first: repo, cloud, project, shared, system. A tier is a memory store of the standard layout in a directory (defaults under the qargi root; memory.tiers in the project answers moves any of them) or, for cloud, the project's memory store. qargi memory tiers [--json] lists them with their state and note counts; qargi memory check runs the canon check on each tier that exists and fails when a note path is present in two tiers (README, INDEX and the like repeat per tier by design). The reference store is not a tier. Nothing is written to a tier; creating and moving notes between tiers, and the session hook composing them, come later.
  • Agents write verified facts only under their own role folder of the memory store; shared/ is curated and reached by promotion (qargi canon promote --approved) or by the person, and an agent proposes a shared note in its report. The cloud preamble, the store README, the lead contract, the build role and skill and the canon say so. canon audit still reports only cross-role writes, so an agent writing under shared/ is not yet detected.
